Page.title: Privacy Policy
Page.metaDescription: Privacy policy for Zenvora. Explains data collection for free resources and communications.
Page.content:
Zenvora respects your privacy and is committed to protecting the personal data of our students and visitors. This Privacy Policy outlines our practices concerning information collection, usage, and safeguarding.

### 1. Information We Collect
We collect minimal personal data that you voluntarily submit to us:
- Contact & Suggestions: Your name and email address when you submit lecture suggestions or inquiries.
- Resource Access: Information provided when requesting student starter repos, templates, or roadmaps.

We do not collect sensitive payment information or sell personal data to third-party data brokers.

### 2. How We Use Your Information
We use your information strictly for legitimate educational platform functions:
- To respond to your questions, student feedback, and lecture suggestions.
- To grant access to requested developer cheat sheets and starter code.
- To maintain platform security, monitor server health, and prevent spam submissions.

### 3. Cookies & Local Browser Storage
We use minimal, standard browser storage:
- Essential Session State: To preserve active preferences and verify student resource access across return visits.
- Admin Authentication: Secure session tokens for authenticated administrative portal management.

You can modify your browser settings to decline cookies at any time, though some interactive features may require basic cookies to function.

### 4. Third-Party Links & Embedded Services
Zenvora features embedded content and outbound links to reputable third-party platforms, such as YouTube for video playback and GitHub for open-source repositories. We encourage you to review the privacy policies of external services when leaving our platform.

### 5. Data Rights & Contact
You have the right to request access to any personal data we hold about you or request its permanent deletion. To exercise your privacy rights, email our team at contactzenvora9@gmail.com.

Opportunity.title: Flipkart GRiD Tech Challenge
Opportunity.summary: Flipkart's flagship campus engineering competition offering real-world e-commerce problem statements, PPI interviews, and substantial cash prizes.
Opportunity.content:
### What is Flipkart GRiD?
Flipkart GRiD is Flipkart's annual flagship campus challenge for engineering colleges across India. Now in its successive editions, the competition challenges young engineers to solve real problems encountered in high-scale retail technology, supply chains, generative artificial intelligence, and robotic automation.

### Competition Tracks
The challenge typically splits into multiple tracks:
- **Software Development Track:** Microservices, high-throughput pipelines, and distributed databases.
- **Information Security Track:** Threat modeling, zero-trust architectures, and application security.
- **Robotics Track:** Autonomous mobile robots, warehouse vision systems, and automated sorting algorithms.

### Why It Matters for Engineering Students
Winning or advancing to the finale of Flipkart GRiD provides one of the most reliable and merit-based routes to secure a Pre-Placement Interview (PPI) for Flipkart's Software Development Engineer (SDE-1) positions, with compensation packages among the highest in the Indian tech ecosystem.
Opportunity.eligibleDegrees: B.Tech, B.E., M.Tech, Dual Degree, MCA
Opportunity.eligibleBranches: All Engineering Branches (CSE, IT, ECE, EE, Mechanical, etc.)
Opportunity.minQualifications: Enrolled in an eligible graduation/post-graduation course graduating within the designated batch cycles.
Opportunity.keyBenefit: Pre-Placement Interviews (PPI) for Software Engineer roles + ₹1,50,000 Winner Prize
Opportunity.benefits:
• Direct Pre-Placement Interview (PPI) shortlists for Software Development Engineer (SDE) roles at Flipkart.
• Total prize pool typically exceeding ₹5,00,000+ across national winners and runner-ups.
• National finalists receive Flipkart merchandise, mentorship from Principal Architects, and tech talks.
• Fast-track evaluation bypassing initial resume screening rounds.
Opportunity.prerequisites: Data structures and algorithms, system architecture, distributed computing, or AI/ML depending on chosen track (e.g. GenAI, Smart Robotics, Information Security).
Opportunity.howItWorks:
1. Level 1: E-commerce & Algorithmic Online Quiz testing core CS fundamentals, problem solving, and logical aptitude.
2. Level 2: Project Submission Round where teams choose an official problem statement and submit an architectural design and proof-of-concept prototype.
3. Level 3: National Grand Finale where shortlisted teams demonstrate their working application and code to Flipkart's senior engineering leadership.
Opportunity.prepGuide:
### Topics to Master
- Scalable backend architectures, caching (Redis), message queues (Kafka), and database indexing.
- Machine Learning models for recommendation, computer vision, or natural language processing.
- Clean code practices, modular design, and robust API contracts.

### Actionable Preparation Steps
1. Form a complementary team of 2-3 members (e.g. one strong in algorithmic problem solving, one in full-stack architecture, and one in AI/system design).
2. Review past years' GRiD problem statements published on Unstop (formerly Dare2Compete).
3. Prepare a high-quality GitHub repository with complete documentation, architecture diagrams, and a working demo video.
Opportunity.applyProcess:
1. Visit the official Flipkart GRiD portal on Unstop during the annual announcement window.
2. Form your team and ensure all members verify their college email IDs.
3. Complete registration before the Level 1 online quiz commences.
Opportunity.tips:
• Team balance is critical: Ensure at least one member is adept at rapid prototyping while another focuses on system design trade-offs.
• Judges look closely at scalability: Clearly explain how your solution handles millions of concurrent shoppers during festive sales.

Opportunity.title: Amazon HackOn
Opportunity.summary: Amazon's premier nationwide hackathon challenging students to innovate customer-centric technological solutions with direct interview opportunities for Amazon SDE roles.
Opportunity.content:
### About Amazon HackOn
Amazon HackOn is a nationwide collegiate technology contest organized by Amazon India. It provides students an opportunity to build solutions that embody Amazon's culture of customer obsession and operational excellence.

### What Makes HackOn Unique?
Beyond prizes, Amazon uses HackOn as an elite talent identification pipeline. Top-performing participants routinely bypass initial recruiting steps and are evaluated directly for Software Development Engineer (SDE) internships and full-time campus appointments.

3. Prototype Development & Mentorship: Teams build working software prototypes with feedback from Amazon technical mentors.

### Core Skills to Prepare
- Data Structures: Arrays, Trees, Graphs, Dynamic Programming, and Hash Tables.
- Cloud Technologies: Familiarity with AWS services like Lambda, S3, DynamoDB, or EC2 is a strong differentiator.
- Amazon Leadership Principles: Be prepared to articulate *Customer Obsession*, *Bias for Action*, and *Invent and Simplify* in your design decisions.

Opportunity.title: Smart India Hackathon (SIH)
Opportunity.summary: The Government of India's flagship nationwide innovation initiative where students solve real-world challenges submitted by central ministries, state departments, and industries.
Opportunity.content:
### About Smart India Hackathon
Smart India Hackathon (SIH) is a nationwide initiative launched by the Ministry of Education's Innovation Cell (MIC) and AICTE. It is widely considered one of the largest hackathons in the world, engaging hundreds of thousands of students annually in solving governance and public service technology hurdles.

### Two Major Editions
- **Software Edition:** 36-hour non-stop coding competition focused on software systems, mobile apps, web applications, and analytics.
- **Hardware Edition:** 5-day intensive prototype fabrication challenge for robotics, medical devices, renewable energy, and smart sensors.

Opportunity.eligibleBranches: All Engineering, Technology, and Applied Science Branches

Opportunity.minQualifications: Regularly enrolled students at an AICTE / UGC recognized institution with college SPOC approval.

Opportunity.keyBenefit: ₹1,00,000 Cash Prize per winning Problem Statement + Government Ministry Recognition
Opportunity.benefits:
• Direct national recognition by Government of India Ministries and AICTE.
• Cash prize of ₹1,00,000 for each winning team per problem statement.
• Potential incubation and grant support for outstanding working prototypes.
• Travel allowance and full accommodation provided at national nodal centers during the Grand Finale.
Opportunity.prerequisites: Full stack web/mobile development, IoT/embedded systems (for hardware edition), database architecture, or applied AI/ML.
Opportunity.howItWorks:
1. Internal College Hackathon: Colleges conduct internal screenings to nominate their top teams.
2. Problem Statement (PS) Selection: Teams select an official PS released by Central Ministries or PSU industries.
3. Idea Submission & Evaluation: PPT proposal and architectural diagrams submitted via the official SIH portal.
4. 36-Hour Non-Stop Grand Finale: Shortlisted teams travel to assigned national nodal centers across India to build and test their product non-stop.
Opportunity.prepGuide:
### How to Build a Winning SIH Solution
- **Functional Completeness:** A working MVP with real database transactions always beats a slide deck with mockups.
- **Offline Resiliency:** Many government problem statements (agriculture, disaster relief, rural logistics) require solutions to operate with low or intermittent internet connectivity.
- **Role Division:** Assign dedicated roles: 2 Backend engineers, 2 Frontend/Mobile developers, 1 Database/DevOps engineer, and 1 Pitch/Presenter.

1. Form a 6-member team ensuring at least one member is female.
2. Approach your college AICTE Single Point of Contact (SPOC) for internal nomination.
3. Submit the proposal PPT on the official sih.gov.in portal.
Opportunity.lastVerified: Verified for Smart India Hackathon Annual Cycle
Opportunity.tips:
• Do not overlook the mandatory female team member rule: submissions lacking gender diversity are automatically disqualified at the portal level.
• Focus on user experience tailored for non-technical government officials and citizens.

Opportunity.title: Google Summer of Code (GSoC)
Opportunity.summary: A world-renowned online mentorship program that pairs student developers and open source beginners with mentors from global open source foundations.
Opportunity.content:
### What is Google Summer of Code?
Google Summer of Code (GSoC) is an international online program focused on bringing new contributors into open source software development. Contributors work with an open source organization on a 12+ week programming project under the guidance of mentors.

### Understanding Open Source Contribution
Open source software powers everything from operating systems and web browsers to databases and artificial intelligence libraries. GSoC teaches students how real-world software is built collaboratively across time zones, with continuous integration, unit testing, and rigorous code reviews.

Opportunity.geographicRestrictions: Worldwide (subject to standard international trade laws)
Opportunity.minQualifications: 18+ years of age at registration. Must be an open source beginner or enrolled in an educational program.
Opportunity.keyBenefit: Competitive USD Stipend (Adjusted by Purchasing Power Parity) + 1-on-1 Foundation Mentorship
Opportunity.benefits:
• Financial stipend based on country purchasing power parity (typically $1,500 to $3,000+ USD).
• Weekly direct mentorship from senior developers at Apache, Linux, Blender, Python, CNCF, and Mozilla.
• Permanent contributor recognition on the official Google Summer of Code archive.
• Major resume asset that fast-tracks software engineering interviews worldwide.
Opportunity.prerequisites: Git, GitHub workflows (PRs, issues, code review), and proficiency in at least one language relevant to the chosen organization (Python, C++, Java, Rust, Go, TypeScript).
Opportunity.howItWorks:
1. Mentoring organizations apply and are announced by Google.
2. Contributors review project lists, join organization communication channels, and submit introductory pull requests.
3. Contributors draft detailed technical proposals outlining milestones, architecture, and weekly delivery schedules.
4. Accepted contributors write code across standard (12 weeks) or extended project timelines with mid-term and final evaluations.
Opportunity.prepGuide:
### Practical Preparation Guide
- **Start Early:** The single biggest mistake students make is waiting for the proposal window to open. Start contributing to organizations 2–3 months beforehand.
- **Public Communication:** Never direct-message mentors asking for project ideas. Introduce yourself on public mailing lists, Zulip, Discord, or Slack channels and ask thoughtful questions about existing open issues labeled *good first issue*.
- **Write Modular Code:** Submit small, clean, test-covered pull requests rather than giant code dumps.
Opportunity.applyProcess:
1. Browse accepted organizations on summerofcode.withgoogle.com.
2. Pick 1 or 2 organizations matching your technical skill stack.
3. Make meaningful contributions to the repository.
4. Submit your proposal document via the official portal before the annual closing deadline.
Opportunity.tips: • Merged pull requests before proposal submission are the single most influential factor in mentor selection. Show that you can already work with the codebase.
